2609.11532.title: Prompt Revision as a Source of Cultural Bias in Text-to-Image Systems
2609.11532.paper_summary: Commercial text-to-image systems silently revise user prompts before generating images, a step users typically cannot disable or even see. Yet, existing audits of cultural bias examine only the final images and treat generation as a single pipeline, so they cannot tell where the bias originates. We introduce WORLDVIEW, a multilingual benchmark of 8,960 prompts across 15 languages and 31 language-context pairings. Using it, we audit the revision layer in three systems (DALL-E-3, Imagen-4, GPT-Image-1.5) through a three-step analysis of how heavily it marks each cultural context, whether it flattens that context into a narrow vocabulary, and whether that vocabulary is stereotypical. Relative to a no-context English baseline, the US is the least-marked context, while non-Western and non-Anglophone contexts are marked far more heavily, flattened into narrow vocabularies applied across topically diverse prompts, and reduced to recognizable cultural stereotypes. Comparing images from original versus revised prompts on models without a revision layer, we identify the layer itself as a previously undocumented, causal source of this stereotyping. To locate cultural bias, and fix it, we must audit the system as deployed, not the model alone.
2609.11532.paper_summary_zh: 商業文本到圖像系統在生成圖像之前靜默地修訂用戶提示，這一步驟用戶通常無法禁用或甚至看到。<lb/>然而，現有的文化偏見審核僅檢查最終圖像，並將生成視為單一流程，因此無法判斷偏見的來源。我們介紹了WORLDVIEW，一個涵蓋15種語言和31種語言-上下文配對的8,960個提示的多語言基準。<lb/>利用它，我們通過三步分析對三個系統（DALL-E-3、Imagen-4、GPT-Image-1.5）的修訂層進行審核，分析其在多大程度上標記每個文化上下文，是否將該上下文壓縮為狹隘的詞彙，以及這些詞彙是否具有刻板印象。<lb/>與無上下文的英語基準相比，美國是標記最少的上下文，而非西方和非英語國家的上下文則被標記得更加明顯，壓縮為應用於主題多樣的提示的狹隘詞彙，並簡化為可識別的文化刻板印象。<lb/>通過比較在沒有修訂層的模型中原始提示與修訂提示的圖像，我們將該層本身確定為這種刻板印象的先前未記錄的因果來源。<lb/>要定位文化偏見並修正它，我們必須審核已部署的系統，而不僅僅是模型。
